title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 26 (Matters to Be Stated in Prospectus)

content.overview: Section 26 prescribes the content and formal requirements of a prospectus issued by or on behalf of a public company, including specified disclosures, dating, signing and filing with the Registrar.
content.glance: List disclosure heads; note dating, signing and ROC filing; flag SEBI overlay for listed issues.
content.study: A prospectus must be dated and signed and must state the information and reports specified by the section and the rules. A signed copy must be filed with the Registrar for registration before the prospectus is issued. SEBI regulations apply in addition where securities are listed or proposed to be listed. Current-law framing: treat s. 26 as the core disclosure statute for public offers under the Companies Act, read with SEBI where applicable.

sections.heading: Statutory Content
sections.body: The prospectus must contain the matters and reports prescribed by the section and rules.

sections.heading: Dating and Signing
sections.body: The prospectus must be dated and signed by the persons named as directors or proposed directors.

sections.heading: Filing with Registrar
sections.body: A signed copy must be delivered to the Registrar for registration before the prospectus is issued.

sections.heading: SEBI Overlay
sections.body: Listed and intending-to-list issues must also satisfy SEBI disclosure regulations.

provisions.title: Matters to be stated in prospectus

examples.title: Compliant prospectus
examples.body: A public company dates and signs its prospectus, includes prescribed disclosures, and files a signed copy with the ROC before issue.

examples.title: Issue without filing
examples.body: A prospectus is circulated without prior delivery of a signed copy to the Registrar. Section 26 is breached.

hypotheticals.question: Is dating alone enough?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 26 also requires prescribed content, signing and ROC filing before issue.

distinctions.title: Content of prospectus (s. 26) vs deemed prospectus (s. 25)
distinctions.left: What must be stated and filed
distinctions.right: When an offer-for-sale document is treated as a prospectus

misconceptions.trap: A short advertisement is always enough without a full prospectus.
misconceptions.correction: Public offers require a prospectus meeting s. 26 requirements, subject only to specific statutory exceptions.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 26 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the prospectus. II. Check content, dating, signing and ROC filing. III. Apply SEBI if listing involved. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Disclosure checklist; formality compliance; SEBI status; precise relief.

examTips: Always mention ROC filing before issue.
